html:
The Gurjara-Pratiharas ruled much of north India from about 730 to 1036. At their height in the 9th century their empire reached from Gujarat to Bihar and was the strongest state in the subcontinent.

The dynasty rose in Rajasthan and Malwa. Its first great king, Nagabhata I, beat back Arab armies raiding out of Sindh about 738, which stopped the Arab advance into India for almost three centuries.

For two hundred years the Pratiharas fought the Palas of Bengal and the Rashtrakutas of the Deccan (see Chalukyas and Rashtrakutas) for the city of Kannauj, the prize of the Ganges plain since Harsha. Historians call it the Tripartite Struggle. The Pratiharas won the city about 816 and made it their capital.

Under Mihira Bhoja, who ruled about 836 to 885, the empire was at its peak. The Arab merchant Sulaiman wrote that this king had the best cavalry in India and was the greatest enemy of the Muslims.

A Rashtrakuta raid sacked Kannauj in 916. The governors then broke away one by one and became the Rajput kingdoms. Mahmud of Ghazni took Kannauj in 1018, and the last king died about 1036.
sum: The Gurjara-Pratiharas ruled much of north India from about 730 to 1036. At their height in the 9th century their empire reached from Gujarat to Bihar and was the strongest state in the subcontinent.
